clue.text: Bores backing flag comprehending talks

indicators.note: backing means the assembled letters are read from back to front
comprehending means taking in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to flag is to tire, to sag
gabs means talks idly

explanation.surface: Tedious people waving a flag backwards while following some negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the verb, to droop or tire, not a banner, and 'Bores' are tiresome people rather than drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasbags are people who talk too much, and such windbags are proverbial bores.

clue.text: Best ever look? Revolting beards!

parts.note: GOAT is slang for the greatest of all time

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: A boast about the finest look ever, undercut by a disgusted verdict on the beards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' is not disgust but a turn-over signal on SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed tuft of hair on the chin, a style of beard.

clue.text: Page secured by older office appliance

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the next word's letters

parts.note: staler means older, less fresh

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper fixed in place by some ancient piece of office kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler is a desk device that fastens sheets of paper together with wire staples.

clue.text: Capital chap supporting upset mother

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed underneath the other part
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A capital fellow propping up his distressed mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan.

clue.text: Learned about cold anger and outrage

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer word encloses the rest

parts.note: a sage is a learned person
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: A scholar holding forth on frosty fury and indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is a noun's adjective here standing in for SAGE, a wise person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something sacred, an outrage against what is revered.

clue.text: Choose chips, reportedly, for outdoor meals

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, so the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: to pick is to choose and nicks are chips, giving PICK NICKS when spoken

explanation.surface: Choosing fried potatoes, it is said, for meals eaten outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips are small nicks or notches, not fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten in the open air, often on a rug in a park.

clue.text: Place impeccable skiers teach essentials for starters

definitions.text: Place impeccable skiers teach essentials for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Where flawless skiers instruct beginners in the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters spell the word, and the whole clue describes it too: the ski slope is where top skiers teach novices.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared ski run, the place where skiing is taught and practised.

clue.text: Unappealing Conservative, innocent perhaps

parts.note: something innocent is harmless, perhaps

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who is dull and maybe blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking charm means having no attractiveness, so unappealing is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Puck takes measures leading to consequences

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream, an imp
acts are legislative measures

explanation.surface: A hockey puck's handling leading to outcomes on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck is not ice-hockey kit but Shakespeare's fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacts are effects or results, the consequences something has.

clue.text: One buried inside watery grave

indicators.note: buried inside means placed within the letters of the next word

parts.note: serous means watery, like serum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone interred in a waterlogged tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective meaning solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious are synonyms describing a weighty, solemn manner or situation.

clue.text: Bloodless returning spooks keeping nasty

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse
keeping means holding inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency, whose agents are spooks
mean means nasty

explanation.surface: Pale ghosts coming back while harbouring something unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooks are spies, not ghosts: CI + MEAN + A reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic means lacking healthy red blood cells, hence pale and figuratively bloodless.

clue.text: One under canvas by second romp

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a camper sleeps in a tent, under canvas

explanation.surface: A tent-dweller frolicking around a moment later.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about playfully, which is what a romp involves.

clue.text: Plant, say, with method trapping insect

parts.note: EG (for example) is what say means

indicators.note: trapping means enclosing, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a line is a method or approach, as in a line of attack
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A plant, for instance, with a technique for catching bugs, like a flytrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose shrub, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Virile male before a detailed cut

indicators.note: before means this piece comes first in the answer
detailed means losing its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: A manly fellow getting ahead of an intricate haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as elaborate, but it means de-tailed: CHOP without its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively masculine behaviour, a strong virile image.

clue.text: Desire follows small rise

indicators.note: follows means this part comes after the next one

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A longing that comes after a modest increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden upward movement, a rise in level or amount.

clue.text: List some asset, a remuneration raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
some means only part of the words is used, a stretch sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Itemise part of an asset, a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETAREMUNE sits across 'asset, a remuneration' and is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to name items one by one, which is to list them.

clue.text: Snack otherwise includes cool seconds

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: else means otherwise
even means calm or cool-headed, as in even-tempered

explanation.surface: A snack that might feature something chilled and a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack of tea or coffee and a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light refreshment taken around eleven in the morning, a snack.

clue.text: Transient, our agenda involves train

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A passing scheme of ours that brings in a railway service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway word but means a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can be a body of followers attending someone important, which is an entourage.

clue.text: Reckless forward taking on defender, finally

indicators.note: taking on means taking in, so a letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: forward means cheeky or impudent

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rash striker tackling a full-back at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: forward is the adjective for bold, and only the last letter of defender is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise and heedless of risk, a close synonym of reckless.

clue.text: People dressed like a monk

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to people a place is to live in it
second meaning: read as ..., wearing a monk's robe

explanation.walkthrough: 'People' is the verb, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit is to occupy as a resident; split in two it describes wearing a religious robe.

clue.text: Zero space round artist turning model

indicators.note: turning means turned round, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: no means zero, none

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a gap is a space
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: No room around a painter spinning a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + GARAP reversed; 'model' is the ideal, not a catwalk figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence to follow.

clue.text: Haggard character facing Queen is simple

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so this piece comes first

parts.note: She is the title character of H. Rider Haggard's novel
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A worn-out figure confronting the monarch is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like gaunt but is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose She is about an immortal queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means pure or unmixed, as in sheer folly, so it is simple.

clue.text: European inclined to purchase grand chic

indicators.note: to purchase here means to grip, so one word holds the letter

parts.note: leant means inclined
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A continental keen to buy something stylish costing a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase is grip or hold, as in getting a purchase on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, which is what chic describes.

clue.text: Stayed with socialist, taking direction

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the word holds another inside

parts.note: a red is a socialist
a side is a direction, as in on that side

explanation.surface: Remained loyal alongside the left-winger, picking a path.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live somewhere, so resided means stayed or dwelt.

clue.text: Gather, we hear, to see band

indicators.note: we hear means listen to the word spoken aloud

parts.note: to hoard is to gather and store up

explanation.surface: Assemble to watch a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical but is a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or gang, a band of people.

clue.text: Legion lacking imperial official?

parts.note: a count was an official of the Holy Roman and other empires
less means lacking, without

explanation.surface: A Roman army unit missing an emperor's officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' is not the Roman unit but the adjective for very many.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means very numerous, so they are too many to number.

clue.text: Affairs about gutted suitors embracing sweetheart

parts.note: CA (circa) means about

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one part goes inside the other
gutted means emptied of its insides, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Romances involving devastated wooers hugging their darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismay but leaves only the outer letters, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cases and affairs both mean matters or business, as in 'that is my affair'.

clue.text: Subject of work kept in check, mostly

indicators.note: kept in means held within the next word
mostly means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tick is a check mark
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A matter of labour held largely in restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter being discussed, a subject.

clue.text: Spongers in pubs consuming pickled snack?

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: bars are pubs
a pickled egg is a traditional British pub snack; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Freeloaders in the local tucking into a jar of pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickled eggs, kept in jars on the counter, are an old British pub snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggars live by asking others for money or food, which is what spongers do.

clue.text: Double over after endlessly happy praise

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other
endlessly means both ends are cut off
over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: dual means double

explanation.surface: Twice as much acclaim following an endlessly cheerful time.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap in approval, hence to praise or commend.

clue.text: Plays with dog, head to tail

indicators.note: head to tail means the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a dog is a dud or flop, a stinker

explanation.surface: Someone playing with their pet, nose to tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog is slang for something poor, a stinker; its head S moves to the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle or make small adjustments, so tinkers means plays with.

clue.text: Moved left welcoming China's leader

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the letter sits inside the word

parts.note: exited means left

indicators.note: leader means the first letter

explanation.surface: Departed, after greeting the head of the Chinese state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' is the emotional sense, stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Moved can mean emotionally stirred, and excited means roused in feeling.
